messages.author: 3c04c342136fe2e7
messages.subject: Next (baby) steps: Common blog?
parts:
Having worked with the two previous GSoC iterations, I had a chance to go the
end-of-summer wrap up sessions at Google. That was a good opportunity to
learn from other organisations about what works, what helps, ...

And one lesson seems to be to keep communication flowing. Some organisations
even enforce weekly reports between students and mentors. I was hoping that
we could do something a little less formal. How would folks feel about, say,
a joint wiki page or maybe a joint blog?

So maybe one of the students could register a new blog at one of the free
services like blogger, wordpress, ... and then (off-list) share the
credentials with the other four. That way we would end up with one place to
go for status updates and flow of information. It may even allow for
'comments'.

But that is just me thinking out aloud. We could also use the R Wiki, or
mail summaries. Thoughts? Comments?

These next few weeks are meant to sort some of these things out. If there
are other questions or suggestions please do not hesitate and bring'em on!

--
Regards, Dirk

messages.subject: Re: Next (baby) steps: Common blog?
parts:
Hi dirk, Roger and the others.

Here are two suggestions that might be of use:
1) Any blog service can offer a "subscribe to new posts by e-mail" service through: feedburner.com
(Services like wordpress.com, offer this built in)
2) Wordpress.com has a (free) very interesting service which is "post by e-mail".
After activating it, you get a secret e-mail address (to send out to the students).  When you e-mail that address it will post your e-mail to the blog (including images and some other attachments - .txt files are, I believe, fine)
Using this service could simplify the reporting process while keeping it transparent, public and open for (public) comments.

If either point requires help or clarification I would happily assist.

Best,
Tal

messages.author: 3f3060000990daa6
messages.subject: Re: Next (baby) steps: Common blog?
parts:
Hi,

I'd like to step in the discussion and take the opportunity for a short introduction:

My name ist Felix Schönbrodt, I'm a PhD student working at the Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich (Germany).
I'm very happy that my GSoC proposal got accepted - I'm working with my mentor Stefan Schmukle on social relations analyses (a topic mainly relevant for psychologists and social sciences). Thanks to Dirk and all mentors for the effort put into the organization of the GSoC projects.

Concerning the "information flow", some thoughts of mine:

I see 4 possible target audiences for the information flow:

Internal communication:
1. Between students and mentors: I think, information between student and mentor should be set up according to their individual preferences
2. Between all current GSoC students: Students could inform each other about the current status of their own project and give mutual motivation

External communication:
3. Towards Google: "See how productive we are, and how successful we mentor and accomplish our projects. Next year, you can give us more of them ;-)"
4. Towards the R community: "Look, we have some very active and talented students, wisely guided by generous mentors. We are a great community. Check out the new projects!"

Personally, I am going to use R-Forge and the built-in mailing list for the internal communication of my project.

For points 2 - 4, I think a blog which documents the milestones of the 2010 projects (Which projects got accepted? Which were the major steps and obstacles? And a documentation and celebration of the results at the end of the period) would be a nice thing. Maybe it would be nice if it's integrated in the rest of the R infrastructure (e.g. in the R-Wiki), instead of setting up an "unconnected" external blog?

Concerning 4), an article in the R Journal would be nice.


Best,
Felix

messages.author: 7d2d2f522132a5e1
messages.subject: Re: Next (baby) steps: Common blog?
parts:
Hi all!

Following Felix's lead, I'll first introduce myself.

I'm Chidambaram (chillu) and I'm a student of Electrical Engineering at IIT, Kharagpur (India) working towards a Bachelors in Electrical and Masters in Control Sytems Engineering. I'm working with Prof. John Nash on building an Automatic Differentiation Engine in R.

And really a big thanks to Dirk for his dedication and patience (especially with me!).

I agree with Felix, in that the communication between the mentor and student is the most important and it should be in a form that both are comfortable with. In our case we have opted to use a wiki.

OTOH, it is also important to keep the community informed about important milestones so that people can know when the project has reached important milestones and is ready to be tinkered with. For this purpose I think its best to have a common blog where all the 2010 GSOC students from R can post so that the people from the R community can visit *one* place for all the updates relating to the GSOC projects. Possibly they can subscribe to the RSS feeds and keep themselves updated on the latest from the projects. (One could also argue that the R mailing lists are already the one place that R devs visit regularly and GSoC milestone announcements could be made here itself)

I think its important that we sort this out before the 20th of May, so that actual communication can take place subsequently in a form that everyone agrees on.

Regards,
Chillu
